summary: Made LoRA CPU metadata allocation conditional on the target platform's pinned-memory capability in all LoRA layer offset sites and the torch_native backend. The original unconditional pin attempt was reproduced before the patch. Focused CPU tests now execute torch_native LoRA without any pinned allocator and match an independent numerical reference. A real CPU-engine server loaded a deterministic tiny Llama and its LoRA adapter and passed the original startup point, but this ROCm-prepared environment failed during the first request in an unrelated CPU RoPE path, so end-to-end HTTP generation and the reported Qwen3-VL Xeon workload remain unverified.

tests.command: /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-0e4b6528890e/venv/bin/python inline baseline reproduction with TorchNativeLoRABackend(device=cpu) and a rejecting Tensor.pin_memory
tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before regression: prepare_lora_batch raised RuntimeError: no pinned memory allocator is available at torch_backend.py's unconditional .pin_memory(). Raw output: reports/j-0e4b6528890e/raw/baseline_reproduction.txt

Three CPU tests: adversarial no-pinned-allocator coverage for layer offsets and torch_native batch metadata, plus exact torch_native A/B output equality against an independent matmul reference. Raw output: reports/j-0e4b6528890e/raw/cpu_unit_tests.txt
Broader LoRA unit regression suite: 82 passed, 6 skipped, and 14 subtests passed. Raw output: reports/j-0e4b6528890e/raw/lora_unit_suite.txt

On AMD Instinct MI355X, accelerator-target metadata remained pinned and torch_native LoRA output matched an independent matmul reference with maximum absolute error 4.76837158203125e-07. Raw output: reports/j-0e4b6528890e/raw/gpu_numerical_reference.txt

Real CPU-engine serving attempt using --enable-lora --lora-backend torch_native. Model and adapter loaded and startup passed the pin-memory failure point; first inference was blocked by NameError: apply_rope_with_cos_sin_cache_inplace in the prepared ROCm stack's CPU RoPE path. Raw log: reports/j-0e4b6528890e/raw/cpu_server.log
Formatting tool availability; the pinned interpreter does not contain the ruff module. git diff --check was used instead and passed. Raw output: reports/j-0e4b6528890e/raw/ruff.txt

remaining_limitations: No Intel Xeon AMX node or accelerator-free PyTorch build was available. CPU behavior was tested on CPU tensors with all pin attempts made fatal, plus a real CPU-engine process in the pinned ROCm environment.

The real CPU HTTP request did not complete because the prepared ROCm software stack selected a CPU RoPE path whose apply_rope_with_cos_sin_cache_inplace symbol was undefined. This is outside the LoRA pinning change and prevents claiming complete serving-path validation.

Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct weights and the user's image-captioning adapter were unavailable. The deterministic tiny Llama fixture validates loading, transport/startup, and engine entry only; it does not validate Qwen3-VL architecture support, multimodal semantic accuracy, AMX performance, or distributed execution.
No native source was changed, so no native library rebuild was applicable.
The pinned interpreter does not provide ruff; syntax, focused pytest, GPU numerical execution, and git diff whitespace checks were used instead.
